targets.title: Relative Education and the Advantage of a College Degree.
targets.evidence_quote: The claim selected for reproduction from Horowitz (2018) is that while individuals with college experience use verbal skills more than those without a college background do, this advantage declines as the proportion of college-educated individuals increases.
targets.outcome_computational_quote: This fails to replicate the original result. Some features of the regression are similar to the original: the sign and significance of all of the non-interacted degree proportion and education terms shown in the above table, as well as the interaction between degree proportion and Some College, No Degree match, and the 𝑅 2 value of . 326 is similar to the . 339 in the original paper. However, the coefficient on the interaction term between degree proportion and BA degree is of an opposite sign to what was expected by the replication criteria.
targets.outcome_robustness_quote: The claim selected for the original study yielded a negative regression interaction term in the focal test, corresponding to an increased local degree proportion reducing the effect of holding a four-year degree on the use of verbal skills. The replication yielded a positive regression interaction term in the focal test, corresponding to an effect in a different pattern compared to the original study.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The re-created analysis of the same source data produces comparable numerical output but reverses the focal interaction. Independently reconstructed occupational matching, outcome factor construction and inclusion rules change the substantive finding, providing robustness challenges. No numbers directly copied from the original author data were needed for comparable output.
